title: Share one embedded copy of Sequencer.js instead of a Scheduler Agent specific Sequencer.js.dat
description:
Registered on the owner's request of 2026-11-15; to be decided and done later.

Today the Scheduler Agent keeps its own generated copy of the sequencer library: indigo_drivers/agent_scheduler/Sequencer.js.dat is produced by the rule in indigo_drivers/agent_scheduler/Makefile.inc (hexdump of indigo_drivers/agent_scripting/library/Sequencer.js), checked in, regenerated by an Xcode build phase and included into indigo_agent_scheduler.c as the sequencer_js[] array, which the agent sends to the Scripting Agent through AGENT_SCRIPTING_RUN_SCRIPT when SEQUENCE_STATE is not defined yet. indigo_server builds a second, separate resource copy of the same file at build time (indigo_server/Makefile, indigo_server.c), and indigo_test/Makefile references the .dat too.

Problems with the scheduler-specific copy: every change of Sequencer.js must be followed by regenerating a checked-in file in another driver's directory, a forgotten regeneration makes the scheduler load an older library than the repository has, the generated single line ends with a space and needs a whitespace exception (.gitattributes '*.dat -whitespace', added by ticket ad64a613), and the library is embedded twice in a server that loads both.

Proposed: keep one shared copy of the library and let the Scheduler Agent use it instead of creating its own. Options to evaluate: the Scripting Agent owns the embedded library (as it does boot.js.dat) and offers a way to load it on request, so the scheduler only asks for it; or a single generated artifact shared by the Scripting Agent, the Scheduler Agent and indigo_server. Decide where the copy lives, how the scheduler triggers the load when the Scripting Agent has no sequencer yet, how a library already loaded by a client is treated, and how the build (Makefile.drv, Xcode, Visual Studio projects, static server build) and the tests find it. Update SCHEDULER.md ('Running a task'), the README notes if the owner approves, and the tests that rely on the scheduler loading the library.
